subject: Hosted evaluation: onramp sprint scope & rate expectations
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finflux.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation: onramp sprint scope & rate expectations

Hi Sanjay —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed small onramp sprint so we can validate Hosted API fit quickly:

- What we heard: FinFlux prefers fastest time-to-value and wants to avoid heavy infra lift up front. Primary concerns were sustained throughput for realtime scoring, burst handling for peak trading windows, and SOC2/data-retention for transaction-level logs. You flagged potential later need for Private/VPC if there are strict residency or on-prem restrictions, but for now the team wants to trial Hosted.

Proposed Hosted onramp sprint (2 weeks):
- Sandbox endpoints: chat (conversations) + embedding endpoint (vectorization)
- Initial rate guidance: target sustained ~50 req/s, burst to 200 req/s for short windows (we can tune based on traffic profile)
- Token/budget guardrails: we’ll provision token caps per endpoint for the pilot and surface per-token cost estimates in the console
- Deliverables: sandbox endpoints, basic observability dashboard, and a short SOW for procurement

Ask of you: can you share a realistic traffic sample (per-minute request counts + average tokens/request) and procurement contact for SOW/PO? If you can, please attach the CSV you mentioned on the call.

I attached a starter SOW outline and a traffic profile template for convenience. If this looks good we’ll lock a kickoff for Mon 10/18 and provision the sandbox ahead of time.

Attachments: finflux_sow_draft.pdf (stub), traffic_profile_csv.csv (stub)

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finflux.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finflux.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: onramp sprint scope & rate expectations

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the clear recap. A few notes from our side: 

- We are comfortable starting with Hosted for the pilot — speed is the priority.
- We did mention potential PHI-like restrictions for a subset of flows; for now that’s limited to the clearing pipeline and we believe pseudonymization will suffice for the trial. We’ll surface strict residency/VPC requirements if legal pushes back.
- See attached traffic sample (first pass). The CSV includes 7 days of per-minute counts and token averages for our customer-facing scoring endpoint. Peak windows are typically at 09:30–09:45 ET and 16:00–16:15 ET; sustained outside peaks is ~30–60 req/s.

Procurement note: procurement@finflux.ai will need the SOW + an estimate for monthly committed spend for the pilot (even if short term) so they can open a PO.

Quick Qs:
1) Can Redwood guarantee a burst policy that covers the peak windows you saw?
2) What telemetry is retained by default (request logs, token counts) and can we toggle retention to meet our compliance policy?

I’ll loop in our security lead if we need to dig into SOC2 evidence.

Best,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Product, FinFlux

Thanks for the sample, Sanjay — that’s very helpful. A couple answers and an adjusted plan: 

1) Burst policy: we can provision an initial rate cap profile that supports sustained 50 req/s and short bursts to 200 req/s. For the pilot we’ll implement traffic shaping and request-level retries with exponential backoff to smooth peaks. If you need guaranteed hard limits for SLAs we can discuss Dedicated capacity as the next step, but for the trial Hosted should cover your peak windows with the profile above.

2) Telemetry & retention: by default Hosted keeps anonymized request metrics and token counts for 90 days and request-level logs (headers + sanitized payload) for 30 days. We can adjust retention windows per account (shorter or longer) and support redaction/pseudonymization options. For SOC2 evidence we have an auditor packet available — we’ll share the link and can schedule a call with our security lead if needed.

Updated actionable plan: 
- I’m attaching a SOW draft tailored for a 2-week pilot with acceptance criteria (latency < 200ms p50 for chat endpoint, correctness checks on 50 eval prompts).
- Ops will provision two sandbox endpoints (chat + embeddings) by Fri 10/15.
- We’ll set initial rate caps as noted; Ben will handle provisioning and health checks.
- Procurement ask: if procurement can provide a PO or a contact we’ll attach a commitment estimate (pilot commit) to the SOW.

Possible kickoff: Mon 10/18 — please confirm availability.

Attachments: finflux_sow_draft.pdf (updated), traffic_profile_csv.csv

Regards,
Tessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Sanjay — looping in ops detail.

Ben here — I’ll provision the sandbox endpoints today and post test endpoint URLs to the Drive folder. For clarity on what we’ll expose for the pilot:
- chat endpoint: /v1/endpoints/finflux-chat-test (conversations + functions allowed)
- embed endpoint: /v1/endpoints/finflux-embed-test (embedding outputs only)
- initial quotas: 50 rps sustained per endpoint, 200 rps burst window (30s)
- token budget: 1.5M tokens/day aggregate for pilot (we can raise if needed)

We’ll also enable request-level telemetry for 30 days and provide a short runbook for how to interpret the metrics. I’ll add a short post to the Drive folder with test curl examples and a small Postman collection.

If procurement sends the PO to procurement@redwood.com we’ll attach the SOW and finalize pilot billing.

Cheers,
